links.reason: Verse 135 shows Yugi's purpose to part the queen (சிலதினம் பிரிவிக்கச் சிந்தைகூரத் தோன்றினான்), matching the plan of 129, but it says nothing of a second bride, which the teaches sentence adds. The sense of the last line is itself uncertain.

The two do connect (2001 says she would not look even on Kama; 908 makes Civakan her one exception), but that is a limit on the vow, not a tension, and nothing in 908 says the dare was 'settled' or an 'open door'.

Pattinathar's verse puts good and evil under what the lotus-born wrote (பங்கயத்தோன் எழுதாப்படி), while Saccandan says birth and death come from தம் வினைப் பயத்தின்: a real difference of cause. But the gains claim that the king's view leaves worship useless is not in 269, which never mentions worship.

Kural 1233 has the shoulders announce the parting (தணந்தமை அறிவிப்ப); in 1522 she asks them where he went (எவ்வழியே கினன்), so they are not a record of union and parting. The shared image is real but the note overstates it as both making the shoulders the record.

Both verses set a birth reckoning that fixes a husband (1686 சாதக முறையிற் செய்தார்; 1451 விதியின் எண்ணி), a real parallel. But the teaches claim about licensing the hero's many brides as fate is a pattern read across, not shown by these two verses.

1659 only begins the pounding song and sings of the dark one (கரியவனைப் பாடினார்); it gives no content of his fame. This is sequence, and the teaches sentence about war and love in the song is not in the verse.

The hunters' maxim (காட்டுண் அமக்கு வலியாரையும் காண்டும்) is answered by 453 where their bows are cut and they vanish. A claim refuted by a scene is a sound shape, but the note says Civakan destroys the six thousand where the verse says மாய்ந்தார், vanished or perished, flagged uncertain, so the note overstates.

304 has the kings paying tribute in fear (திறைகொடுத்து) before the girl appeared; 305 says since her birth he has stopped taking it (திறைகொளல் ஒழிந்து). The later verse reverses the earlier, and the teaches sentence is true of both.

The narrator's வினைவிளை காலம் ... தேரான் ஆகி and Kannaki's தேரா மன்னா with ஊழ்வினை துரப்ப do put the same failure to inquire under karma and under guilt. The pair shows both causes held together; the note is accurate on both ends.

Bhavachutan says he saw a fault (ஊனங் கண்டேன்) and will speak (உரைசெய்கேன்); the Kural says the one at the king's side must speak. But the fault is in Asvagriva, and the verse does not say he speaks against a colleague's counsel as the teaches and gains clauses claim; it is an illustration.

PN 25 asks whether the spear 'did not stop short' at the sight of widows, which the marker itself calls uncertain; 2221 only says the widows put off adornment and the spear smoked. It does not count widows as the spear's foreseen price, and the gains clause about rare restraint has no ground in either.

Kural 902 says one who desires a woman and neglects other things earns shame; 67 says the queens set the work of guarding aside, binding the king's mind. A real shared theme, but the narrator does not blame, and the gains clauses about a verdict are muddled.

196 has the brahmins bless the dead king for the upper world after eating the kid; 197 has the kid recall its birth and know the ruler as its son. The rite's claim is answered inside its own scene, as the teaches says.

577 gives the astrologer's saying that the maiden's life lies on earth (மாதர்வாழ்வு மண்ணதே); 563 gives the king's pearl-and-conch saying. Nothing in the Tamil shows the second was 'turned' from the first, so the causal claim rests on a reconstructed order.
359 puts the question to the council and 382 has the astrologer say the girl's matter is weighed. This is story sequence, and the teaches sentence is only that.

Kural 796 makes ruin the rod that measures kin (கிளைஞரை அளப்பதோர் கோல்); Nanmanikkadigai 3 lists the tests of gem, horse and gold, ending கெட்டறிப கேளிரான் ஆய பயன். The verse sets the same idea in a sequence of assays, so the pair shows ruin as a test.
Neither verse names Indra on the shared image: 25 has Indra, 144 does not. The link rests on a commentator's story, which the brief rules out, so the Tamil does not support it.

14 names the elephant that frightened Gunamalai and Civakan's victory; 1076 shows that elephant shamed (அஞ்ஞான்று ஓடிய நாகம் நாணி). But the usurper's pretext and the mahout's report in the teaches sentence are not in 1076.

1866 calls the Lord foe of deluding deeds (மருள்புரி வினைகட்கு மறுதலை) and Kural 5 says the two deeds do not cling; a real overlap, but 'two ways of reading freedom' is only a theme, and the gains clauses are generic.

Both name the dark-handed smith (கருங்கைக் கொல்லன்), but in 170 he is only the simile for the anvil, in 180 he is asked to forge a spear. The teaches claim that his forge links fighting and giving is the note's construction.

1355 warns that women will shun fleeing men; PN 278 has the mother rejoice at her son's wounds after swearing to cut her breast, so the contrast of threat and test is real. But the gains clauses are muddled and attribute the sword and rebuke to the wrong sides.

1083 has Death in the woman's eyes (கூற்றென்பதனை இனியறிந்தேன்); 637 calls her girdle and breasts கூற்றம். The shared image is real, but 'told and not saved' and the crowd's staying are not in the Tamil.

1175 calls the minister the king's understanding and eye (உணர்வுங் கண்ணும்), which is near Kural 445, but the note rests on his question rather than that. The teaches sentence is thin and the Kural's 'take counsel' is a different point.

வரைவின்றி in 107 and வரைவிலா in Kural 919 share a word, but the epic only describes the courtesans' quarter and the Kural condemns them; a shared word is no tension. The epic verse does not praise the trade either.

2073 shows அறத்தொடு நிற்றல to the friend, a real akam convention that Kuruntokai 333 has the heroine propose to her friend (தோழி vocative, not the friend asking). The chain to foster mother, mother and father is not in the verse.
1696 has the king give gifts on seeing the letter and 1698 gives its content, which is plot order; there is no incompatible claim, so tension is wrong and the teaches sentence is only sequence.

309 has women tempt the king as his vow begins, and 310 has him cross the sea of delusion (மோகத்தில் ... நீந்தி), then the elephant shaking off its fetter. The link reads the elephant as an image, which the marker says is unsettled; the temptation answered by the crossing is the sounder link.

281 forbids the king to take his own life (நின்னுயிரை நீ களையின்); Kural 327 says give up one's life rather than do a deed that takes another's. The verse does not 'extend' the couplet; they are different cases, and the gains clauses are muddled.

259 sends Vegavati to break Madanamanjikai's firmness; 261 has Vegavati herself take desire (காமங் கூர்ந்து). A reversal of the plan, which is a sound shape, but tension is the wrong type and the desire's subject is flagged uncertain.
729 has Civakan's song shame Kama (அனங்கன் நாணப் பாடினான்); 2037 says he seems the god of spring. The shared figure holds, but the shift from open victory to covert seduction is not in either verse.

250 says the king's fire burns those who touch it with their kin (தீண்டினார் தமைத் தீச் சுடும் ... கிளையொடும்); Kural 691 says be neither far from nor near the fire (தீக்காய்வார்). The epic carries the image from distance to punishment for touching, as the note says.

Soolamani 1559 shows pleasure without judgement (காமனே கலவிக்கின்றான்); Naladiyar 60 judges it. Without a claim in the epic verse there is no incompatibility, so this is a contrast of stance, not a tension.

Kural 678 is about using one task to do another, with a rutting elephant to take an elephant; 40's wooden elephant of men is a ruse, not that rule. 'King as the catch' is not in the verse, so it rests on the shared elephant.

Kural 1115 jokes that her waist will break under anicham with its stems; 679 says she shuns flowers (பூச்சாரச் செல்லாள்) lest her small waist break, and spectators lament those who dressed her (பாவம்). The same conceit moves from a lover to a crowd.

402 foretells Ashvagriva's loss of life and discus; 619 shows him lost in pleasure (அச்சுவ கண்டன்). The irony is the reader's own, and the verse only names him; the link depends on the marker's reading of earlier verses.

217 says no rule without such men (இன்னவரின்றி இலை அரசு); Kural 445 says the king should take counsellors after counsel, with counsellors as his eyes. 217 does not say counsellors are his eyes, so the gains clause is added.

Naladiyar 47 names the fool's address (பெருந்தோளி பெய்வளாய்) to a body of nine openings; 987 has the king marvel at beauty. But 987 is a figure of praise and the work does not claim that view, so there is no incompatible claim.

252 says failed counsel turns on the king like a snake; Kural 448 says a king without those who rebuke him perishes. Different failures, and the note's 'instrument turns on user' is the epic's claim, not a limit on the couplet.

260 names the twins and the younger son (அபயருசி, அபயமதி); 73 has the youth speak of knowing his births. That the twins are the cocks reborn is not in 260, and the teaches sentence, itself inferential, contradicts the marker's own note.
1764's blessing of rain and crops (தண்புனல் பயிர் விளைக) matches Kural 545's பெயலும் விளையுளும், but a blessing is not a claim on the king, and nothing in the verse says so.

Kural 1102 says she is the cure of the sickness she causes; 1332 says only the sandal on her breasts heals the wound her eyes made. A real parallel, but the timing after union rests on the marker's reading.

624 is a reported claim by the astrologer that a self-conqueror is hard to conquer (தன்னை வென்ற வேந்தனைப் பிறர்க்கரிது); Tirumanthiram 140 is about the senses coming under control after meeting the Lord. The shared theme of self-mastery is all the pair has.
2622 has Vijayai urge giving; 2829 only promises to tell the fruit of gifts (கொடைப்பயன் அறியக் கூறுவாம்). It states no content, so 'two halves of one argument' is the note's reading.
